title: Enhancing Short-Text Topic Modeling with LLM-Driven Context Expansion and Prefix-Tuned VAEs
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
task: Topic modelling of very short texts
problem: Short texts lack word co-occurrence; expanding them with an LLM helps but can shift meaning and is slow at inference.
architecture: Step 1: LLAMA2 expands each short text into a longer text. Step 2: PVTM, a smaller language model trained with prefix tuning and coupled with a VAE, infers topics from the short text and is trained to reconstruct the LLM-expanded text, so expanded texts are needed only for training.
key_results: Running LDA on LLM-expanded texts raises CV from 0.399 to 0.523.
TagMyNews, K = 20: PVTM CV 0.632 vs CTM 0.618.
Classification on StackOverflow, K = 50 (SVM): 0.825 vs CTM 0.814 on short texts; CTM drops to 0.656 on expanded texts, showing topic drift.
strengths: Uses LLM knowledge without needing the LLM at inference time.
Separates topic quality from topic faithfulness via classification.

limitations.text: LLM generation can be noisy and out-of-domain; PVTM does not fully solve extreme sparsity (TagMyNews).
Not best everywhere: e.g. Google News K = 20 LR accuracy 0.569 vs TSCTM on expanded texts 0.699.
